name: Pinhole surgical technique (gum recession)
lead: The pinhole surgical technique (PST) is a minimally invasive procedure for gum recession in which a small hole is made in the gum above the recession and specialised instruments are used through it to loosen the gum tissue and move it over the exposed root, without cutting or suturing a graft. It was described in a 2012 retrospective study of 43 consecutive patients with 121 recession sites, as an alternative to connective tissue grafts whose second surgical site causes morbidity.[1]
Subsequent case series and randomised trials have tested it alone and with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) or collagen membranes, but the published studies reviewed are small.[2][3][7][10]

paras: The technique was introduced as a response to the donor-site morbidity of free connective tissue grafts, which are described as the most predictable root-coverage method.[1] Case series from India describe it as part of a minimal-invasion concept in periodontal plastic surgery.[2][7]

The 2012 retrospective study examined PST in 43 patients with 121 sites, 85 of them Class I recessions.[1] A split-mouth randomised trial of 18 patients combined PST with advanced PRF and compared it with a resorbable collagen membrane.[3] Other studies tested PST with and without A-PRF in multiple adjacent recessions[5] and with and without PRF in a randomised trial.[9] Case reports and series describe PST with propolis[6] and a cone-beam CT study assessed alveolar bone changes after minimally invasive surgery.[8] A 2024 meta-analysis addressed A-PRF in gingival recession generally.[4] Registered trials compare PST with connective tissue graft[10] and with the tunnel technique,[11] and test PRF additions.[12]
The sources reviewed are mostly case series, small trials and one retrospective study, and numerical outcomes are not summarised here.

timeline.event: The pinhole surgical technique is described for root coverage.[1]
An Indian case series reports PST in five cases.[2]
A split-mouth trial compares PST with A-PRF and collagen membrane.[3]

card.summary: A keyhole gum-recession procedure that repositions tissue without a graft; small studies, limited long-term data.
card.note: Evidence is mainly case series and small trials.

quick.overview:
The pinhole surgical technique treats receding gums through a small opening in the gum rather than by harvesting a graft from the palate. It was described in 2012 as a less invasive option.

Available studies are small case series and trials, some adding platelet-rich fibrin or collagen membranes.
quick.mechanism: Instruments passed through a pinhole loosen the gum tissue so it can be moved over the exposed root, with or without added biomaterials.
quick.risks: The reviewed sources do not detail complication rates. Evidence is limited to small studies and one retrospective series.
